summary.headline: Fabtech FY26 total income rose 28.4% to ₹431.33 crore, but margins compressed; management guides ~25% growth and 9.9–10.5% PAT margin.
summary.overview: FY26 total income grew 28.4% YoY to ₹431.33 crore and EBITDA rose 18.29% to ₹55.56 crore, while reported net profit fell to ₹38.36 crore from ₹46.45 crore (FY25 included ₹17.85 crore exceptional item). Q4 total income rose 22% YoY to ₹168.24 crore and quarterly net profit rebounded to ₹22.06 crore. Margin pressure was attributed to remobilisation, a 33% rise in RMC cost and a 43% rise in execution cost, amid Middle East disruption. Cash and bank balance rose to ₹208.57 crore after a ~₹230 crore equity infusion (IPO), while receivables rose to ₹204.34 crore.

segments.name: UAE
segments.commentary: Largest market; revenue grew by about ₹126 crore (₹126.6 crore) in FY26, with two subsidiaries in Dubai.

segments.name: Saudi Arabia
segments.commentary: Revenue at about ₹82.7 crore in FY26, with a subsidiary, a JV and a local entity; vaccine and animal-health projects won.

segments.name: Kenya / Africa
segments.commentary: Kenya revenue grew by ₹43.24 crore; West and North Africa wins include a $7.05 million tablet/capsule facility in West Africa and a ~₹49–52 crore EU-GMP veterinary facility in North Africa.

segments.name: Mark Maker (33.33%)
segments.commentary: Management says this investee, a process OSD and closed-loop line division, is contributing to growth.

guidance_outlook: Management projects ~25% revenue growth (Karan Doshi cited 25–30%), with 'close to 25% or more' in closing remarks.
PAT margin targeted to improve toward 9.9%–10.5%; internal targets are contribution margin ~45%, EBITDA margin 13–14%, PAT margin 9–11%.
Order book above ₹900 crore as of March 31, 2026, to be executed over 18–24 months.

Management says it is on track for the 12–14% PAT guidance for FY28 (per Rahil's question); FY27 revenue of ₹530–600 crore from earlier conferences was not reconciled, with the difference attributed to consolidated versus standalone communication.
Q1 FY27 completion targeted for the North Africa veterinary facility.
capex_capacity: Strategic equity infusion of ~₹230 crore (IPO) to fund expansion; part earmarked for talent acquisition; the JBN acquisition in the West is under due diligence and not yet closed.
Local infrastructure in UAE and Saudi Arabia, with on-ground installation teams; in-house manufacturing covers process, air, water, containment and clean room partitions.
Stakes: 100% subsidiaries in UAE (FTS) and Saudi Arabia (Fabtech Saudi); 33.33% in Mark Maker; 16% in TSA (water systems); 49% in FABL (containment).
Pre-engineered buildings and solar integration being added to control project timelines; greenfield project timelines reduced by ~20% from 24–27 months.
Related-party procurement: ~11% of clean room panels from FTCL and ~15% of air handling units from Advantek.
demand_pricing: Order book above ₹900 crore as of March 31, 2026, including Dubai operations; split across UAE, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Kenya, other Africa and North Africa (Algeria, Morocco, Egypt, Ethiopia).
Hot-lead pipeline of about $200 million with offers in the market; bid-to-win conversion stated at 11%, rising to 16–17% of hot leads.
Order sizes increasing: earlier $30–40 million, now orders up to $70 million; some orders above ₹50–60 crore.
Q4 top line about ₹150 crore; highest sales in March.

Pricing: contracts USD-denominated (LC-backed), with variation clauses for raw-material and freight cost increases. Contribution margin was 43.8% vs 45.9% prior year; RMC cost grew ~33% and execution cost ~43%.
Revenue recognised on Bill of Lading submission against LC; billing is lumpy and dependent on client civil readiness.

qa_highlights.question: Why have margins shrunk despite revenue growth, and how will investor confidence be regained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited project and geography mix (Africa margin pressure), remobilisation, a ~33% RMC cost increase and ~43% execution cost increase; non-contribution margin at 43.8% vs 45.9% last year. Margins expected to improve as internal margin development progresses.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Middle East conflict on Q4 and expected impact going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: No material financial impact per management; freight is the main cost pressure while RMC is sourced in India and revenue is in USD. Delivery delays are possible; no cancellations so far, and clients are discussing variation clauses.

qa_highlights.question: How are raw-material and freight increases reflected in customer contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Contracts contain variation clauses, with post-detailed-engineering items priced at net present value; management says clients accept variations to avoid project delays. It is not a pass-through, but a negotiated outcome that also affects future awards.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakdown of the ₹900 crore order book by geography and the timeline for conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Split across UAE, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Kenya, other Africa and North Africa; to be executed over 18–24 months. Billing depends on client readiness to accept materials and complete installation.

qa_highlights.question: Why was IPO fund deployment delayed, and what is the plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it an active decision: the JBN acquisition in the West is under due diligence and talent acquisition is ongoing. Monitoring agency required ₹50 crore working-capital reimbursement to come from the monitoring account, which is now being done. Current borrowings are USD PCFC lines at about SOFR-linked rates plus 200 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin target and guidance for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal targets: contribution margin ~45%, EBITDA 13–14%, PAT 9–11%. Management said it remains on track for the 12–14% FY28 PAT guidance, with FY27 growth of about 25%.

risks_watch: Margin compression: contribution margin 43.8% vs 45.9%; RMC and execution cost inflation, with Africa projects carrying lower margins.
Receivables of ₹204.34 crore (Dubai ~₹37 crore, Saudi ~₹61 crore), with management guiding to collection-led discipline; Q4 billing concentration will unwind only in Q1–Q2.
Geopolitical exposure: Middle East war affecting logistics, visas and site access; project delays on greenfield civil works, though no cancellations reported.
Order conversion timing: booking to billing gap; 18–24 month execution of ₹900 crore order book; hot-lead conversion of 11%–17%.

IPO fund deployment pending: JBN acquisition under due diligence; monitoring agency compliance issues; reconciliation of FY27 revenue guidance (₹530–600 crore from earlier conferences) versus ~25% growth commentary.
Related-party dependence on FTCL (~11% of clean room panels) and Advantek (~15% of air handling units).
summary.management_tone: Confident and defensive: management stressed resilience, order book visibility and the 'War Team' execution record, but was evasive on specific FY27 revenue targets and on the reason for margin compression, attributing it to mix and cost factors.
key_quotes: We are not a quarter-to-quarter story. We will stand by our yearly guidance.
Our focus is clear not growth at any cost, but growth with a strong profitability and sharper capital efficiency and discipline scale.
Until we see the money or smell the money, we don't go after announcements.
It is more of a combination of a portfolio mix.
